IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.         OF 2026
(arising out of SLP(Crl.) 10518/2026)
VIJENDER KUMAR ..... APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
STATE OF RAJASTHAN & ANR. ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. The appellant, Vijender Kumar, is aggrieved by the interim
order dated 02.12.2024 passed by the High Court of Judicature
at Rajasthan at Jodhpur1 in S.B. Criminal Revision Petition Nos.
1145 and 1269 of 2024, filed by Yashpal @ Yash Bhambu and
Rajveer @ Rajkumar Bhambu respectively, staying the proceedings
in Sessions Case No. 28/2021 on the file of the learned
Additional District and Sessions Judge 2, Bhadra, Hanumangarh,
Rajasthan.  It is the case of the appellant, that the revisions
have been pending since then and owing to the stay order, the
proceedings in Sessions Case No. 28/2021 have remained stalled.
3. The case relates to the alleged harassment of the victim,
Ravinder Kumar, which led to his suicide on 05.08.2021.  In that
connection, First Information Report (FIR) No. 205/2021 dated
07.08.2021 was registered on the file of Police Station –
1  “High Court”, for short
2  “ADSJ”, for short
Crl.A. @ SLP(Crl.) No. 10518/2026 1

--- Page 278 ---
Bhirani,  District  –  Hanumangarh,  Rajasthan,  for  offences
punishable under Sections 306, 384 and 143 of the Indian Penal
Code, 18603. The accused named therein were five in number, viz.
Hanuman  Poonia,  Prem  Kasniya,  Rajveer  Bhambhu  @  Rajkumar
Bhambhu, Yash Bhambu and a private School Director. Upon
completion  of  the  investigation,  a  chargesheet  was  filed
against the accused for offences under Sections 306, 384 and
120B of the IPC.  The case was committed to the Sessions Court
and was taken up by the learned ADSJ.
4. While so, the accused filed an application therein seeking
discharge under Section 227 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973. However, by order dated 23.07.2024, the learned ADSJ
rejected their application and framed charges against them
under Sections 306, 384 and 120B of the IPC.
5. It is this order that was subjected to challenge before the
High Court in its revisional jurisdiction in S.B. Criminal
Revision Petition Nos. 1145 and 1269 of 2024 by two of the
accused, Yashpal @ Yash Bhambu and Rajveer Bhambhu @ Rajkumar
Bhambhu. The revision petitions are stated to be still pending
consideration by the High Court. Meanwhile, the High Court
deemed it appropriate to stay the proceedings in Sessions Case
No. 28/2021, by its order dated 02.12.2024.  The validity of
the said order is presently in question.
6. Perusal of the impugned order reflects that the High Court
opined that even if the acts alleged against the two accused,
3  “IPC”, for short
Crl.A. @ SLP(Crl.) No. 10518/2026 2

--- Page 279 ---
Yashpal @ Yash Bhambu and Rajveer Bhambhu @ Rajkumar Bhambhu,
were taken on face value or even in entirety, it would be
difficult to constitute an offence under Section 306 of the IPC
and stayed further proceedings in Sessions Case No. 28/2021
against Yashpal @ Yash Bhambu and Rajveer Bhambhu @ Rajkumar
Bhambhu till the final disposal of the revision petitions.  
7. What is patently clear from the aforestated order is that the
High Court did not consider the fact that a separate charge had
been framed against the accused with regard to extortion, under
Section 384 of the IPC, and even if the charge in relation to
abetment to suicide under Section 306 of the IPC was in doubt,
the separate charge under Section 384 of the IPC warranted
examination independently.  There was, therefore, no cause for
the High Court to stay further proceedings altogether, thereby
bringing the proceedings to a grinding halt.
8. The appeal is, accordingly, allowed, vacating the stay and
setting aside the impugned order dated 02.12.2024 passed by the
High Court in S.B. Criminal Revision Petition Nos. 1145 and
1269 of 2024.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO.       OF 2026
(arising out of SLP(C) No. 16025/2025)
RAJENDRA ..... APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
PRABHAVATI & ANR. ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. The  appellant,  Rajendra,  challenges  the  oral  order  dated
06.11.2024 passed by a learned Judge of the High Court of
Karnataka,  Dharwad  Bench,  in  Civil  Revision  Petition  No.
100060/2020.  By the said order, the learned Judge modified the
order dated 07.06.2018 passed by the learned III Additional
Senior Civil Judge and Chief Judicial Magistrate, Belagavi,
dismissing Ex. Case No. 79/2017 and held that the appellant,
Rajendra, was entitled to refund of 50% of the amount, in terms
of Clause 7 of the Compromise Decree dated 17.08.2012.
3. By order dated 23.05.2025, this Court issued limited notice on
the quantum of the refund payable to the appellant.
4. It is an admitted fact that, in terms of Compromise Decree
dated 17.08.2012 passed by the learned II Additional Senior
Civil Judge and Chief Judicial Magistrate, Belgaum, in Original
Suit No. 38/2011, the appellant failed to pay and clear off the

--- Page 282 ---
entire amount on or before 28.02.2013 and, in consequence,
Clause 7 of the said Compromise Decree came into play.  
5. As per the said clause, it was agreed by and between the
parties to the suit that, in the event of non-compliance, the
defendants in the suit, viz., Shri Bharama and Shri Jinnappa,
should refund half of the total amount received by them to the
appellant, the plaintiff in the suit, and retain the remaining
half of the total amount received by them towards damages for
non-compliance with the terms.
6. This being the settled position, the appellant would not be
entitled to anything other than what was provided to him in the
Compromise Decree dated 17.08.2012.  However, we may note that,
in terms of the aforestated Clause 7, the defendants in the
suit had an obligation to refund 50% of the amount received by
them upon non-compliance by the appellant-plaintiff on or
before 28.02.2013. However, no steps were taken by them to do
so after the said date. 
7. Shri Bharama, having passed away, his widow, Prabhavati, and
Shri Jinnappa are the respondents before us, and it is conceded
on their behalf that the refund in terms of Clause 7 has not
been effected till date. We are informed that 25,00,000/-₹
(Rupees twenty five lakhs only) was paid by the appellant-
plaintiff to the defendants in the suit and, in terms of Clause
7 of the Compromise Decree dated 17.08.2012, he was entitled to
refund of 12,50,000/- (Rupees twelve lakhs fifty thousand₹
only). As the defendants/respondents retained the amount, which
was lawfully due and payable to the appellant, for over 13

--- Page 283 ---
years, we are of the opinion that it would subserve the
interest of justice if they refund the said amount along with
reasonable interest at least at this stage.
8. The appeal is allowed in part, directing the respondents to
refund the sum of 12,50,000/- (Rupees twelve lakhs fifty₹
thousand only) to the appellant with simple interest @ 8% per
annum within two months from today. The interest would be
payable till the date of actual payment.
9. Parties shall bear their own costs.
    Pending application(s), if any, stand disposed of.
.....................J.
(SANJAY KUMAR)
.....................J.
(SANJEEV SACHDEVA)
NEW DELHI;
NOVEMBER 06, 2026.

Judicature at Madras in WP No.6376 of 2017 and WP MP
Nos.6882 and 7633 of 2017. The operative portion of the
impugned order reads as under:
“12. Without considering the above points, the
Debts Recovery Tribunal shall not declare the asset
in question as NPA or assign the debt to any ARC.
Thus, the Debts Recovery Tribunal, Chennai shall
consider all these aspects and pass appropriate
orders. Till such order is passed by the Debts
Recovery Tribunal, no coercive action be taken by
the respondent-bank against the petitioner-company.
It is made clear that the petitioner shall remit
the EMI regularly, as agreed without any further
default and also make substantial payments in lump
sum at regular intervals to cover up default amount
to further avoid declaring the property as NPA and
to pay the EMI amount regularly.
13. The writ petition is disposed of accordingly.
No costs. Consequently, the connected miscellaneous
petitions are closed.”
In  the  Special  Leave  Petition  filed  by  the
petitioner before this Court,  vide  interim order dated
27.10.2017 this Court granted stay of operation of the
impugned  order.  Consequently,  the  petitioner-Bank  has
taken steps under the provisions of the Debts Recovery
Tribunal Act, which resulted in passing of the judgment
and decree against the respondent - borrower and on the
basis of the recovery certificate issued by the Recovery
Officer, steps have already been taken for sale of the
2

--- Page 307 ---
mortgaged  property  and  it  is  stated  that  a  sum  of

is pending before the Debts Recovery Tribunal (DRT) for
the purpose of delivery of possession and consequential
orders to be made pursuant to the sale of the mortgaged
property and that there may be other issues also which are
pending consideration before the DRT. 
In view of the subsequent developments that have
been taken place during the pendency of this Special Leave
Petition consequent upon the interim stay of the impugned
order granted by this Court, we do not find it necessary
to go into the issues raised by the petitioner in this
Special Leave Petition as we find the same being rendered
academic. 
Consequently,  we  dispose  of  this  Special  Leave
Petition by noting the aforesaid developments, which have
also been elaborated in the affidavit filed on behalf of
the petitioner, reserving liberty to both sides to raise
all other contentions that are available to them in law
and  without  going  into  the  contention  whether  the
mortgaged property had been rightly declared as a Non
Performing Asset (NPA) or not. 
In  other  words,  the  issue  regarding  mortgaged
property being declared a NPA shall not be gone into in
the further proceedings, which are pending before the
3

--- Page 308 ---
Debts Recovery Tribunal.

the subsequent developments the impugned order has lost
its efficacy and therefore, it is unnecessary to go into

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.           OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) NO.16702/2026)
TINKU DAS @ TINKU KUMAR DAS      APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
THE STATE OF JHARKHAND     RESPONDENT(S)
ORDER
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and
learned counsel for the respondent-State of Jharkhand.
3. Appellant is aggrieved by order dated 17.07.2026
passed by the High Court of Jharkhand at Ranchi (briefly
the ‘High Court’ hereinafter), rejecting the regular bail
application of the appellant.
4. Appellant is an accused in FIR No.30/2026 registered
at  Police  Station-  Deoghar  Cyber,  District-  Deogarh,
Jharkhand under Sections 319(2), 318(4), 338, 336(3),
340(2) and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (for
short, ‘BNS’) and Sections 66B, 66C, 66D and 84(C) of the
Information Technology Act, 2000.
5. Allegation against the appellant is involvement in
cyber fraud leading to fradulent transactions from a large
number of gullible depositors.
1

--- Page 310 ---
6. Appellant was arrested on 25.02.2026 and has been in
custody since then.
7. This  Court  had  issued  notice  vide  order  dated
10.09.2026,  pursuant  to  which  respondent-  State  of
Jharkhand has filed counter affidavit, which we have
perused.
8. We find that investigation is complete whereafter
charge-sheet has been submitted. Though there are no
criminal antecedents of the appellant, nonetheless it has
come on record that appellant had made certain phone calls
which led to fraudulent withdrawal of money from the
accounts of several persons.
9. Be that as it may, having regard to the period of
detention undergone by the appellant and he having no
criminal antecedent, we are inclined to grant bail to the
appellant, subject to certain conditions.
10. That being the position, t he impugned order dated
17.07.2026 passed by the High Court is set aside.
11. Consequently, we direct that the appellant shall be
produced before the Trial Court within a maximum period of
07 days from today, whereafter he shall be released on
bail on such terms and conditions as may be deemed
appropriate.  We  further  direct  that  appellant  shall
furnish an undertaking within two weeks from the date of
release before the Officer in-charge of the Deogarh Police
Station to the effect that he shall not involve himself in
any such alleged activity in the future.
2

--- Page 311 ---
12. Accordingly, the Criminal Appeal is allowed.
13. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

SOUMYAKANTA PATRA & ORS.                           Respondent(s)
O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. Leave granted. 
3. This appeal is directed against the order dated 23.04.2024
passed by the High court of Orissa in W.P. (C) No. 14457 of 2021.
By  the  said  order,  the  respondents  are  held  eligible  for
resettlement  employment  benefit  under  Odisha  Resettlement  and
Rehabilitation policy. The High Court has relied on its earlier
judgment dated 24.06.2022 passed in W.P. (C) No. 1138 of 2013
("Goshibananda Naik vs. State of Odisha & Others).
4. Mr. K.M. Nataraj, learned Additional Solicitor General has
made the singular contention that the decision in Goshibananda Naik
(supra) has no application to the case of the respondents and the
High Court without examining the case of the respondents on merits
1

--- Page 314 ---
D.NO. 281 OF 2025
has relied on its previous decision. Per contra, learned counsel
appearing for the respondents has supported the order passed by the
High Court.  
5. We have considered the rival submissions made on both sides.
From the perusal of the order passed by the High court, it is
evident that the High Court has not examined the rival contentions
of the parties and disposed of the Writ Petition merely by placing
reliance on its earlier decision in the case of Goshibananda Naik
(supra). 
6.  We, therefore, set aside the order dated 23.04.2024 passed by
the High Court in W.P. (C) No. 14457 of 2021 and remit the matter
to the High Court for fresh consideration. Needless to say, all
contentions of the parties are kept open. We request the High Court
to take up the matter and dispose it of as expeditiously as
possible. 
7. Accordingly, the Civil Appeal is disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
SUO MOTO WRIT PETITION(CIVIL)  No(s).  16/2026
1. Apart from the issue concerning the appointment of Judicial
and Technical Members to the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
and National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), this matter
also brings to the fore the deficiencies in infrastructure and the
shortage of supporting staff, which are adversely hampering the
day-to-day functioning of these Tribunals.  
2. It seems to us that the learned Presidents of the respective
NCLTs and NCLAT would be the most appropriate authority to assist
us in addressing these issues.  We therefore request them to submit
a  comprehensive  proposal  outlining  the  infrastructural,
administrative, staffing, and other requirements for strengthening
the functioning of the respective Tribunals. The proposal may also
include the requirements relating to land, building, and the need
for requisite staff. The learned Presidents of the NCLTs shall also
consider the desirability of having an officer of the rank of
Deputy Registrar or Joint Registrar at each Bench for the upkeep
and management of judicial records.  Let all such requirements be
examined by the learned Presidents and their respective proposals
be  placed  before  us.   We  will  appreciate  if  the  requisite
information is forwarded to this Court within four weeks.
3

--- Page 324 ---
3. The Registry is directed to communicate this order to the
learned Presidents of the NCLT and NCLAT.
4. In the meantime, the learned Attorney General for India shall
impress upon the Union of India to ensure that all essential
infrastructure and basic amenities are made available to the NCLT
and NCLAT at the earliest.
5. Post the matter on 10.12.2026
W.P. (Civil)  No(s).    1385/2026
6. Issue notice, returnable on 10.12.2026.
7. Dasti, in addition, is permitted.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The core issue that arises for consideration in these matters
pertains to the constitution and composition of the State Bar
Councils and the Bar Council of India in accordance with the
provisions  of  the  Advocates  Act,  1961  and  the  rules  framed
thereunder.
2. Pursuant to various orders passed by this Court in M. Varadhan
v. Union of India and Anr. , W.P. (Civil) No. 1319 of 2023,
elections to the State Bar Councils have since been conducted.
Additionally  vide orders  dated  04.12.2025  and  08.12.2025  in
Yogamaya M.G. v. Union of India and Ors. , W.P. (Civil) No.
581/2024, it was directed that there shall be 30% representation
2

--- Page 331 ---
for the women members of the Bar in every State Bar Council. Out of
this 30% representation, 20% was to be directly elected, whereas
10% was to be co-opted.  
3. When the issue of the manner and modalities of co-option
arose, this Court  vide order dated 04.08.2026 in  Yogamaya MG
(supra) resolved that the Chief Justices of the jurisdictional High
Courts in consultation with the newly elected members of the
respective State Bar Councils, shall nominate two women members,
preferably from among former women judges of the respective High
Courts or senior women members of the Bar.  
4. It goes without saying that once the co-option exercise is
complete, the composition of the State Bar Councils shall stand
notified. In order to rule out any uncertainty, we therefore deem
it appropriate to request all the Chief Justices to complete the
exercise of co-option within a period of two weeks. The composition
of the newly-elected State Bar Councils shall be notified within
one week thereafter.
5. Following this, each State Bar Council shall be required to
elect its Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, office-bearers as well as
“one member by each State Bar Council from amongst its members” as
member of the Bar Council of India under Section 4(1)(c) of the
Advocates Act, 1961. These elections, therefore, are also required
to be conducted at the earliest. Consequently, we direct the newly-
constituted  State  Bar  Councils  to  elect  their  statutorily
prescribed office-bearers, including their representative to the
Bar Council of India, within a period of two weeks from the date of
notification of their composition.
3

--- Page 332 ---
6. All the State Bar Councils are directed to file compliance
reports in this regard.
7. On  receipt  of  these  compliance  reports,  the  issue  re:
constitution of the Bar Council of India under Section 4 of the
Advocates Act, 1961 shall be considered.
8. Meanwhile, Mr. Maninder Singh and Mr. S. Guru Krishna Kumar,
learned Senior Counsel representing the Bar Council of India and
its office-bearers, have fairly stated that the learned Attorney
General for India and the learned Solicitor General of India shall
be actively associated with the policy-making process leading to
any policy decision that may be taken before the new Bar Council of
India is constituted.
9. Issue notice to all the State Bar Councils.
10. Dasti, in addition, is permitted.
11. Post these matters on 23.09.2026 to await the first compliance
re: completion of the co-option exercise and constitution of the
State Bar Councils.
(NITIN TALREJA)                           (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)

         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PRASANNA B. VARALE
For Petitioner(s) :Mr. Talha Abdul Rahman- 2467, AOR

Upon hearing the counsel, the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner
submits that apart from the lack of opportunity to file a
counter affidavit, there is a procedure contemplated under
the Right to Information Act, 2005 (for short, ‘RTI Act’).
1

--- Page 338 ---
Furthermore, the Writ Petition before the High Court has
been filed pursuant to filing of application(s) under the
RTI Act.
2. It is further submitted that it is not as if the
petitioner is not willing to provide the OMR sheets to the
respondent(s),  but  it  can  only  be  furnished  after
completion of the entire process and the logistics involved
including declaration of the final result, which will take
minimum six to eight weeks. 
3. The learned counsel for the respondent(s) submitted
that considering the facts, the impugned order needs no
interference. 
4. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the
parties, we find force in the submission advanced by the
learned counsel appearing for the petitioner. 
5. In fact, it is the say of the petitioner that the
respondent(s) would be furnished with the OMR sheets only
after the entire process gets completed and considering the
request made at this stage, further process will have a

--- Page 410 ---
2
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Our Order dated 7th September, 2026 reads thus:-
“1. By our order dated 21.1.2026, we had called upon the
respondent-Housing Board to make us understand in what
manner it proposed to rehabilitate the members of the
society, i.e., the petitioners.
2. Today, when the matter was taken up for further hearing,
the learned senior counsel appearing for the Board brought
to our notice that most of the members of the society who
were  unlawfully  occupying  the  subject  land  have  been
rehabilitated as they have availed the benefit of the Scheme
provided by the Board.
3. In the case at hand, there are 38 families who are bit
reluctant to hand over the possession and shift to any other
place.
4. What we have been given to understand is that the
rehabilitation will be at a place called Manali, New Town
Phase -II and the allotment would be subject to deposit of
Rs.10,37,000/-. The Board has also gone to the extent of
saying that, if the members are finding it difficult to
raise the necessary finance, they would help them to avail
the loan facilities.
5. We put a very pertinent question to the learned counsel
appearing for the petitioners whether they have any right,
title or interest to stay at the place in question. The
learned counsel very fairly submitted that they do not have
any right, title or interest.
6. In such circumstances, referred to above, there are only
two options left with the petitioners: (1) to handover the
possession and shift to any other place of their choice or
(2) to avail the benefit of the Scheme of rehabilitation at
the place, referred to above, by depositing the requisite
amount.”
 
2. Today when the matter was taken up for further hearing, the
learned counsel appearing for the petitioner - Society comprises of
members hailing from very poor strata of society submitted that he
has instructions from his clients to make a Statement before this
Court that his clients are ready and willing to avail the benefit
of the Rehabilitation Scheme framed by the Government. 

--- Page 411 ---
3
3. In view of the aforesaid, we permit the petitioners before us
to apply with the competent authority under the Scheme.
4. Once applications are filed, those shall be scrutinized,
verified and all those who are eligible under the Scheme shall be
rehabilitated at the earliest. 
5. We make it clear that while passing orders of allotment under
the Rehabilitation Scheme, there shall be a condition that the
allottee shall not transfer the Flat to any third party or alienate
the same in any manner.
6. We also make it clear that one of the conditions or rather one
of the stipulations in the allotment order should be that in future
if it is found that any of the allottees has sold off the flat or
has alienated the flat in any manner, he shall be criminally
prosecuted for the offence of cheating. It shall be open for the
authority concerned to recover the amount of the value of that flat
at market rate.
7. This entire exercise will be completed within a period of two
months from today.
8. With the aforesaid, this petition stands disposed of.
9. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
 (VISHAL ANAND)                                    (POOJA SHARMA)

CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.       OF 2026
@ SLP (CRL.) NO.19497/2026
PREM KUMAR SINGH                                     APPELLANT
                        VERSUS
THE STATE OF BIHAR                                    RESPONDENT
O R D E R
1. Leave granted. 
2. Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel
appearing for the respondent - State and perused the materials
available on record.
3. As per the averments made in the First Information Report
(FIR), the inducement was given by Rahul Kalra and Anil Kalra.
Allegations against the appellant is that he was a Director in
the company named Washing Express and that certain amounts
were transferred to his account.
4. In similar FIRs being Gandhi Maidan P.S. Case No.201 of
2026, Patliputra P.S. Case No.68 of 2026 and S.K. Puri Case
No.118 of 2026, the appellant has been extended the indulgence
of regular bail by the High Court.
5. In this view of the matter and considering the matter that
the appellant  is in judicial custody for more than five
months,  and  looking  to  the  distinguishable  case  of  the
1

--- Page 443 ---
appellant, we are inclined to grant bail to the appellant on
such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the Trial Court
in connection with F.I.R. No.5117028260214 of 2026, registered
at Police Station Gandhi Maidan, District Patna, Bihar for the
offence punishable under Sections 316(2), 318(4), 336(3), 338
and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
6. Accordingly, the impugned order stands set aside, and the
appellant is granted regular bail, subject to the terms and
conditions that may be imposed by the concerned Trial Court.
7. The appeal is allowed, accordingly.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
           CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
 CIVIL APPEAL NO. 4555 OF 2024 
RAMBIR SINGH & ANR.                      Appellants
                           VERSUS
BHARTI AXA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. & ORS. Respondents
O R D E R 
1. The appeal before us is a challenge against
the  dismissal  of  the  appeal  by  the  Insurance
Company.
2. Learned counsel for the appellants submits
that they have not been granted compensation in
accordance with the decision in National Insurance
Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. reported in
(2017) 16 SCC 680.
3. However, learned counsel for the respondent-
insurance company points out that the appeal was
filed by the insurance company against the order of
the Tribunal, which stood dismissed . Further, t he
cross-appeal filed by the claimants was withdrawn
as is evident from paragraph 9 of the impugned
1

--- Page 446 ---
judgment.
4. We find absolutely no reason to entertain the
present  appeal by  the  claimants  who  did  not
challenge the award of the Tribunal and withdrew
the  cross-objection  filed  by  them  claiming
enhancement. The order impugned in this appeal
confirmed the award made by the Tribunal and only
remanded the matter to adjudicate upon the recovery
of award amounts from the owner of the vehicle,
which  does  not  cause  any  prejudice  to  the
claimants.
5. The appeal is, accordingly, dismissed.
6. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  stand(s)
disposed of.

including Section 112(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

was arrested on 15.04.2026.
4. The petitioner is accused of being involved in an organized
online gambling group, which runs online cricket betting
through  an  app  called  “3  Stumps”,  based  on  disclosure
statements of co-accused.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that several
co-accused have been granted bail by this court. It was
further submitted that the petitioner is not named in the FIR;
implication  was  based  on  alleged  disclosure  statements;
investigation is admittedly complete; and there is delay in
trial, since 38 witnesses are to be examined.

we are of the opinion that the petitioner can be released on

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO(S).              OF 2026
(ARISING OUT OF SLP (CIVIL) NO(S).              OF 2026)
DIARY NO.34272/2026
STATE OF ODISHA & ORS. APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
CITIZENS ACTION FORUM, BHUBANESWAR RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. Leave granted.
3. We have heard Mr. K.M. Nataraj, learned Additional Solicitor
General of India on behalf of the appellant - State of Odisha and
Mr. Matrugupta Mishra, learned counsel on behalf of the contesting
respondent, who is on Caveat.
4. We find from the express language of Rule 12(1)(ee) of the
Minerals (Other than Atomic and Hydro Carbons Energy Minerals)
Concession Rules, 2016 (“Rules”) that the provision is enabling in
nature.  It  confers  discretion  upon  the  State  Government  to
undertake the mining activity where the lessee fails to extract the
mineral in accordance with its obligations under the lease deed. In
such an eventuality, the lessee is liable to reimburse the State
Government, on demand, for all expenses incurred in undertaking
such activity. This provision cannot be construed as mandatory, as
the High Court has done in paragraph 13 of the impugned judgment.  
5. For the reasons aforesaid, the appeals are allowed in part to
the extent that paragraph 13 of the impugned judgment is modified
and it is directed that the State Government shall make an
1

--- Page 488 ---
endeavour in terms of Rule 12(1)(ee) of the Rules for optimum
utilisation of the mines in accordance with law.

         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE NONGMEIKAPAM KOTISWAR SINGH
For Petitioner(s) :  Petitioner-in-person
       
             
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
The petitioner is present in-person. 
The Special Leave Petition has been filed with an allegation
that the petitioner being the injured victim in connection with a
F.I.R. No.27/2017 was pressurized to compromise the matter with the
accused. The High Court quashed the proceedings on the ground of a
compromise arrived at between the parties. The petitioner has
appeared in this Court in person. He is wheelchair bound. He has
submitted that it is a dispute between family member and hence, he
1

--- Page 717 ---
desires to withdraw the Special Leave Petition. 
Having regard to the nature of assertions made in the Special
Leave Petition wherein the petitioner has alleged that he was
pressurized into entering the compromise, we doubly checked with
the petitioner that his prayer to withdraw the Special Leave
Petition is voluntary and free of any coercion or duress. The
petitioner affirmatively states that he is withdrawing the Special
Leave Petition of his own and free will and volition. 
In this view of the matter, the Special Leave is dismissed as
withdrawn.   
(VIJAY KUMAR)                                 (AKSHAY KUMAR BHORIA)

ITEM NO.19               COURT NO.1               SECTION IV-C
               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CIVIL) Diary No(s). 60436/2026
[Arising out of impugned judgment and order dated 18-06-2026 in WP
No. 36057/2025 passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh Principal
Seat at Jabalpur]
UMANG SINGHAR                                      Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH & ORS.                     Respondent(s)
(IA No. 331821/2026 - CONDONATION OF DELAY IN FILING and IA No.
331819/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE IMPUGNED JUDGMENT)
 
Date : 04-11-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JOYMALYA BAGCHI
         HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE V. MOHANA
For Petitioner(s) :Mr. Vivek Tankha, Sr. Adv.
                   Mr. Mareesh Pravir Sahay- 2638, AOR
                   Mr. Lalit Baid, Adv.
                   Ms. Yaman Verma, Adv.
                   Mr. Kartik Jindal, Adv.
                   Mr. Kartik Virmani, Adv.
                   Mr. Vibhor Khandelwal, Adv.
                   Mr. Jayesh Gurnani, Adv.
                                      
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. We have heard learned senior counsel for the petitioner.  
3. We do not deem it necessary to issue notice to the respondents
as no order, prejudicial to their interests, is proposed to be
passed.  From the records, we find that the allegations against
respondent no. 4 are that she voluntarily gave up membership of the
1

--- Page 1035 ---
political party on whose ticket she was declared elected. On this
premise,  it  is  alleged  that  respondent  No.  4  has  incurred
disqualification under the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution.
4. It  further  appears  that  a  petition  seeking  her
disqualification was filed before the learned Speaker of the State
Legislative Assembly on 05.07.2024, but the same has not been
decided so far. The petitioner approached the High Court and, by
the impugned judgment, the Writ Petition was dismissed on the
ground that there was no urgency in the matter.
5. It seems to us that  even where considerable time remains
before the expiry of the term of the Assembly, petitions seeking
disqualification under the Tenth Schedule are expected to be
decided expeditiously, in light of the decision of this Court in
Padi Kaushik Reddy etc. v. The State of Telangana & Ors. etc., 2025
INSC 912.  We, therefore, dispose of this Special Leave Petition
with a request to the learned Speaker of the Madhya Pradesh
Legislative  Assembly  to  decide  the  pending  disqualification
petition expeditiously, preferably within a period of two months.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand closed.
(NITIN TALREJA)                           (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        DY. REGISTRAR
2
